pr_title: fix(rust, python): fix date/datetime parsing for short inputs with exact=False

issue_context.title: `PanicException` for `str.to_date` & `str.to_datetime` with `strict=False`
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
pl.Series(
    name='date',
    values=['2019-01-01', 'ab'], # <<< PanicException
    # values=['2019-01-01', 'a'], # <<< This does NOT Panic
).str.to_date(exact=False)

pl.Series(
    name='datetime',
    values=['2019-01-01 00:00:00', 'ab'], # <<< PanicException
    # values=['2019-01-01 00:00:00', 'a'], # <<< This does NOT Panic
).str.to_datetime(exact=False)
```


### Issue description

`str.to_date` & `str.to_datetime` panic when `strict=False` and text cannot be parsed and has length of >1 it seems

### Expected behavior

normal `ComputeError` with conversion/parsing failed message

thanks for the report

> values=['2019-01-01', 'a'], # <<< This does NOT Panic

doesn't it? ~it does for me~ sorry, it's a `ComputeError:`, not a panic. Can reproduce, will fix
@JulianCologne just for my understanding, what's your use-case for `exact=False`? It's a performance foot-gun, I'd expect it to always be much more performant to clean your data beforehand

review_comments: Is this the gist of the change? That we search in another set?

hey - sorry, I wanted to leave some commentary but it was getting late, I should've left it in 'draft'

The gist of the change is
```diff
-                    for i in 1..(s.len() - fmt_len) {
+                    for i in 1..(s.len().saturating_sub(fmt_len)) {
```
which avoid the panic error

The change in this file is a drive-by cleanup - the formats are duplicated between here and `patterns.rs`, so this reduces the difference between `exact=True` and `exact=False`
